title: Netsh creates a Windows PortProxy rule
description: Detects Netsh or a renamed Netsh binary adding a Windows interface PortProxy forwarding rule.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may add a Windows PortProxy rule to relay TCP connections through a compromised endpoint.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft documents netsh interface portproxy add as the command family for adding TCP forwarding listeners, while MITRE and Atomic Red Team document this mechanism as internal proxy behavior. Requiring Netsh identity and all three full command words is more precise than monitoring generic Netsh or firewall changes.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify Netsh commands that add an interface PortProxy rule while leaving display, deletion, unrelated firewall management and matching text from another executable unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Validate the listener, destination and owner before escalation; WSL, connected-cache, development and administrative workflows can intentionally create PortProxy rules.
steps: Review the complete Netsh command, listen and connect addresses and ports, original filename, parent process, account and endpoint role.
Inspect the active PortProxy configuration and correlate listening sockets, firewall changes, inbound connections and the destination service.
Confirm an approved WSL, cache, development or administration requirement; otherwise remove the forwarding rule safely, contain the endpoint and investigate related network activity.
false_positives: Approved WSL publishing, Microsoft Connected Cache, development testing or administrative TCP forwarding configured through Windows PortProxy

validation.expected_outcome: Match Netsh commands containing the full interface portproxy add sequence; do not match show, deletion, unrelated firewall rules or another executable.
